statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs everything. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 12% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green: a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

The one genuinely material change this hour is a correction to the diplomatic read. The negotiation track is not "still scheduled" - The National reports the latest US-brokered round ended in Rome on 6 August without agreement, divided over Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanese territory, and that subsequent negotiations remain stalled. President Aoun's framing of the strikes as a "clear message regarding the negotiating process" reads very differently against a stalled track than against an upcoming one. The off-ramp that was implicitly being credited is not there.

The rest of the picture hardened rather than cooled. Netanyahu's office now frames the exchange as Hezbollah violating the ceasefire by attacking soldiers in the security zone and seriously wounding three, and says civilians were only later discovered at the struck location; Al Mayadeen reports continued artillery, machine-gun and phosphorus fire on the Ali al-Taher ridge, and southern Lebanese villages are visibly evacuating. Casualties stand at 11 dead across Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani, including three children and two women, with roughly a dozen wounded. A second vector reopened as well: Yemen's government says Houthi missiles killed four civilians in a port city. Hormuz is unchanged and still the structural energy risk - two ADNOC tankers hit by drones on 14 August, transits collapsed to roughly one ship a day against a ~73/day norm, and hundreds of vessels holding position.

Against all of that, Friday's tape was placid: NQ 30,141.75 (-0.15%), the Nasdaq Composite -0.3% but still up on the week, the S&P easing off a record after a third straight weekly gain, the Russell at a fresh record, and VIX at 14.25. That divergence is the whole story, and it does not get resolved until tonight's reopening auction.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing. The roughly 22:00 UTC restart is now firmly inside the forecast window, and it is the single checkpoint that matters: forecast Tail steps to 21% at 22:00 UTC and 23% at 23:00 UTC, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) for the last two slots. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment a full weekend of two-sided Lebanon headlines, a promised Hezbollah response, a stalled negotiation track and an ongoing Hormuz blockade all get priced at once against a 14-handle VIX. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green, but the diplomatic off-ramp is worse than assumed - the Rome round ended 6 August without agreement and talks are stalled - so Stress rises to 70% into tonight's 22:00 UTC CME restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first twenty-two forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 67% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed - a narrow, unremarkable range with no directional efficiency worth scoring. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Fed's own H.15 release at the 13 August observation. The cash tape was equally benign: the Nasdaq Composite closed about 0.3% lower but still finished the week higher, the S&P 500 slipped from a record high while capping a third straight weekly gain, and the Russell 2000 set a fresh record. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way structure. Conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

The new information this hour is diplomatic, and it cuts the wrong way. The previous hour's assessment credited the negotiation track as still scheduled. Read directly, The National's account is that the latest US-brokered round ended in Rome on 6 August without agreement - the two sides divided over Israel's withdrawal from southern Lebanese territory - and that subsequent negotiations remain stalled. That reframes President Aoun's description of the strikes as a "clear message regarding the negotiating process": the message is being sent into a stalled process, not ahead of a scheduled one. Prime Minister Salam rejected the claim that the victims were military targets and said responsibility for any military infrastructure on Lebanese soil lies exclusively with the Lebanese state.

The kinetic picture also hardened. Netanyahu's office frames the sequence as Hezbollah violating the ceasefire by attacking Israeli soldiers in the security zone and seriously wounding three, with the IDF then striking what it identified as a Hezbollah headquarters and only afterwards discovering civilians present. Hezbollah-affiliated reporting describes continued artillery, machine-gun and phosphorus fire on the Ali al-Taher ridge, and residents are visibly evacuating southern villages. Eleven dead in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani, including three children and two women. Hezbollah says the strikes will be "met with what they deserve" - a promised, undelivered response is exactly the kind of overhang that cannot decay while markets are shut. Separately, Yemen's government says Houthi missiles killed four civilians in a port city, and Hormuz remains effectively closed: two ADNOC tankers struck by drones on 14 August, transits down to roughly a single ship a day against a normal ~73, and several hundred vessels holding position off berth.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and stays unobservable for roughly another twenty-one and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress rises to 70% (high) rather than holding or decaying: the stalled-Rome correction removes a de-escalation path that was being implicitly credited, a promised Hezbollah retaliation is still outstanding, Netanyahu's framing is escalatory rather than conciliatory, a second Yemen vector reopened, and Hormuz is unchanged - all against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it and a market with no mechanism to reprice until tonight. Two points is compounding, not panic: this is still a headline stack rather than observed market stress.

The horizon geometry is now fully engaged. At 00:00 UTC Sunday the 24-hour forecast reaches 23:00 UTC, so both the roughly 22:00 UTC restart and the first full hour after it sit inside the window. Forecast Tail therefore drifts 12% to 18% through the halt and then steps to 21% and 23% for the final two slots, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. A thin opening auction absorbing an entire weekend at once is exactly the configuration in which gap continuation can outrun mean reversion. That is a conditional forecast, not an observation: the current published action remains EA_ON and green.

Confidence at 67% (solid) reflects an honest split. Index, volatility, energy and rate marks are verified against primary sources this hour and are internally consistent; the seven-day US calendar was re-read directly from Trading Economics and confirms no high-impact US release before Monday, with the Jackson Hole symposium falling on 27-29 August and therefore outside this window. But the single most informative input for a mean-reversion strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until the restart.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 00:00 UTC to 23:00 UTC Saturday and are entirely inside the weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what actually moved: 45% through the Saturday Asian and early European hours, then climbing steadily at 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67% and 68% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and turned into a two-sided exchange. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 57% to 66% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 23:00 UTC Sunday, so both the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first full hour after it are inside the window. Tail is held in the low band for 22 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 18% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 22:00 UTC and 23% at 23:00 UTC, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 70% to 76% because unpriced weekend risk compounds rather than decays while the venue is shut: a promised Hezbollah retaliation, a negotiation track that has been stalled since the 6 August Rome round ended without agreement, a fresh Houthi strike in Yemen and an effectively closed Hormuz all remain outstanding against a 14-handle VIX. Confidence eases from 67% to 61% as Friday's marks age past eighty hours, then recovers to 63% and 65% once live quotes return at the reopen. The last six slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the entire weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME is shut and stays shut for roughly another twenty-one and a half hours, so there is no price path to score: Tail holds at 12% and the published action stays EA_ON. Stress at 70% carries the weekend's unpriced Middle East stack, not any observed market stress.

Deep weekend dead zone. Nothing can reprice; the only thing that can change is the headline stack. Scores are held flat deliberately rather than manufactured movement, and Confidence eases a point as Friday's marks age.
Asian Sunday morning still has no futures venue open - FX and regional cash are the only tells, and neither is a Nasdaq price path. Tail unchanged at 12%.

Stress keeps grinding rather than decaying, because a promised Hezbollah response, stalled Rome negotiations and an effectively closed Hormuz are all still outstanding with no mechanism to price them.
Confidence slips to 65% as the last live NQ print passes seventy-five hours old. That is an evidence-quality statement, not a risk statement - Tail is still low because the venue is still shut.

Late Asian Sunday. The setup into the reopen is unchanged: benign Friday tape and a 14-handle VIX on one side, an escalating two-front Middle East picture on the other, and no venue to reconcile them until 22:00 UTC.
